title: Mass extinctions
what: The great mass extinctions, where their causes and records lay at the time, and what the studies say caused each.
how: Each extinction is marked within 5 million years of its time: where its cause lay, or a cause held or argued (the Siberian, Emeishan, Deccan and Viluy Traps, the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province, Chicxulub, the Hirnantian ice sheet’s deposits in the Sahara), and where it is dated (the boundary’s reference section). The places are approximate, compiled for this site, and carried back on the PALEOMAP model by the GPlates Web Service. Dates are the milestones’, with their sources. The list itself is argued: the usual five are Raup & Sepkoski’s, Bambach finds only three stand apart, and Rampino & Shen put the end-Guadalupian forward as a sixth, shown here as argued. Where the causes are argued, the card gives each side. Bond & Grasby’s review ties most great extinctions to large igneous provinces. Chicxulub and the end-Permian can be watched in their own time: deep time hands over to their clock as it plays past them at Slow, and offers it faster. The end-Permian’s clock counts from the extinction’s start at Meishan, linearly across the crisis from 400,000 years before to 200,000 after, then by tenfolds to 10 million years after, each phase from the studies that place it. The end-Triassic and the end-Guadalupian can be watched on the same clock, the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province and the Emeishan Traps fuming; the end-Triassic’s four pulses are spread evenly over their 600,000 years, an assumption. The end-Ordovician and the Late Devonian run on a longer clock, a million years before their first pulse to two million after: the Ordovician’s ice sheet growing to its maximum and melting, and oxygen-poor water spreading in patches round the places their records come from, the Kellwasser pulses drawn 150,000 years long, an assumption. The fumes, the ice and the patches are illustrations, not a model: plumes from vents spread over the traps, pale over the flood lavas and dark with the sills’ gas, as strong as the phases say, and a haze over the globe; their heights and sizes are drawn to be seen.
